But it does, last I looked, layer its own repos on top of Arch's to provide for a more stable (sub-)set of packages, if desired.

Having own Arch repos "layer" doesn't make it LTS, it makes it Arch based, and manjaro is a rolling release model same as the Arch distro. LTS is longterm support release model, where software is feature frozen to a specific version, excluding the more critical stuff like Web Browser that updates to latest stable version cause it would be real pain to merge only security fixes from upstream.

It turns out that I misunderstood (and perhaps the linux.com article author did, too) "LTS," when the readme clearly mentions the LTS kernel and not a set of packages of their own choosing and maintenance. I also misunderstood things like "driver support," which sounds like some special set of tested packages kept separate from Arch's packages, but really seems to mean what's included in the Live CD or installer. That could have been clearer.

So I guess they aren't even keeping a set of frozen packages Manjaro-style, since their custom package repo is very anemic. Now I'm even more curious at what makes the distro different, since they obviously have their own installer and desktop configs. Maybe they'll write a blog post about it as it grows or matures. Interesting, nonetheless.

The mentality of the English left-wing intelligentsia can be studied in half a dozen weekly and monthly papers.
